The accountant keeps the books in the accounting SaaS. Gap: the relief pharmacist still works under the owner's account until an own account is set up (due 2026-09-30, POAM-002).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The PMS produces the EPCS internal audit report every day (21 CFR 1311.215(b)), but nobody had ever opened it before 2026-08-06. Starting 2026-09-08 the owner reads the daily EPCS report each business morning and reviews the PMS sign-in report and email sign-in history on the first business day of each month, and logs each review.

Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only PMS administrator, so the audit records stay with the PMS vendor. The PMS protects stored audit records from deletion and prevents modification (21 CFR 1311.205(b)(16)), as confirmed in the EPCS certification report.

Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls with help from the on-call IT consultant. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the pharmacy, such as the IT consultant under BAA, at least every second year. The PMS vendor's SOC 2 and EPCS certification reports, reviewed 2026-08-05, cover the vendor's inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review has not taken place.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; P09 vendor review

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 7.4 limits the PMS administrator role to setting changes. POL-01 6.6 requires the owner to accept, watch, and record each vendor remote-support session in the security log. POL-01 4.3 requires a risk analysis update after a new PMS or a new vendor that handles PHI. The PMS audit trail records every change to its access controls. Gap: the first monthly check of the session log is due 2026-09-30 (POAM-004).

The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the paper downtime kit, the coverage arrangement with a nearby pharmacy, and the sealed emergency access sheet do not exist yet (due 2026-10-31 and 2026-12-31).

implementation_statement: The PMS, e-prescribing, claims, cloud fax, and email services use TLS (inherited). Refill reminder texts contain only the pharmacy name and the words that a prescription is ready, with no drug name.

The owner's CSOS private key signs electronic Schedule II orders. Move it to the owner's own desktop account (or a hardware token if the certificate authority supports it) by 2026-09-30. Report any compromise to the certificate authority within 24 hours (21 CFR 1311.30(e)).
